newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears Dutch PTT buy of TNT.
newsitem.headline: EU clears Dutch PTT buy of TNT.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it had cleared the proposed takeover of Australian transport group TNT Ltd by Dutch PTT Post BV.
The takeover bid also concerns the two companies' joint venture GD Express Worldwide (GDEW), an international courier firm which is also active in express parcel and remail activities.
PTT Post BV is the postal and logistics subsidiary of Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN).
Dutch PTT said on October 2 that it would pay A$2.45 per ordinary share for TNT in a deal valuing the Australian company at about A$2.0 billion.

The Commission said the operation leads to few overlaps in any of the markets concerned. "PTT Post and TNT are both active in domestic express delivery in Germany and in logistics in Belgium, Germany and the Netherlands; but their combined market shares are not significant."

Competitors and customers expressed concern during the Commission's investigation that PTT Post would be able to cross-subsidise from its reserved postal activities and from the reserved telecommunications activities of PTT Telecom BV, which like PTT Post is controlled by KPN, to the activities of TNT and GD Express Worldwide.
"But existing and prospective EU and Dutch legislation largely eliminates these possibilities," the Commission said.
"In addition PTT Post has offered to the Commission undertakings not to cross-subsidise from reserved to non-reserved activities and not to discriminate against competitors," it said.
